channel.title: Roberto Allende
channel.description: AI-first engineering leader and builder based in New Zealand. Notes on technology, leadership, learning, and the work in between.

item.title: [Software] How AWS Hackathons and Challenges Taught Me Not to Vibe Code (and What to Do Instead)
item.description: Over the past year, I've shipped in five AWS hackathons and challenges. Kiro CLI let me move faster than I ever had — but vibe coding still didn't work. Sessions would spiral into hallucination loops I couldn't trace back or recover from. That's what pushed me to micromanage Kiro CLI instead of vibing with it, starting with the AWS Lambda Hackathon a year ago and every initiative since. Working this way not only let me ship a lot more — I've never had to look back.

item.title: [Software] Weekend Agent Challenge: Piano Teacher

item.title: [Software] AIdeas: Lucid Thread
item.description: AI assistants today collaborate on their terms. Lucid Thread gives you twenty specialized AI personas — or build your own. Visible memory. Real-time document tools. All operating within boundaries you design, not boundaries designed for you.

item.title: [Software] Ideas Compound
item.description:
Three years ago I got curious about AI. Not the headlines — the actual thing. What it could do. How it worked.
So I started entering hackathons. Five so far, two more right now.
And somewhere along the way I realized the most valuable thing I built wasn’t any of the projects.
It was something I almost didn’t notice.

item.title: [Software] Five Takeaways from AWS Summit Sydney 2025
item.description: June 4-5, 2025 saw AWS bring together thousands of developers, builders, and business leaders at Sydney's International Convention Centre for their annual Summit. Across 90+ sessions and 80+ partner showcases, the event highlighted both where AWS is directing their efforts and how customers are putting those tools to work Amazon— here are five things that stood out to me from the two days.

item.title: [Software] AI First Imperative: What Does It Mean to Be AI First
item.description: I’ve been practicing an AI First mindset for a few months now. It wasn’t something I defined from the start—it just emerged naturally from how I worked. Whether I was tackling a complex project, debugging a technical issue, or drafting a message, AI became a central part of my thinking loop.

item.title: [Software] AI First Imperative: Preventing Your Digital Kodak Moment
item.description: Imagine standing in a photo lab, holding a freshly printed picture, unaware that the very act of developing film is about to vanish. Disruption rarely announces itself with sirens—it creeps in, reshaping industries before most notice. AI isn’t just another innovation; it’s a tidal wave accelerating change. Will you harness it to stay ahead, or risk falling behind? What happens next is up to you.

item.title: [Software] Free Up Your Time from Email with Amazon Q Apps & GenAI
item.description: Built with Amazon Q Apps in just two hours at the AWS & Ingram Micro GenAI Hackathon in Auckland 2025, Reply.ai is an intelligent email assistant that helps you take control of your inbox.
